factProposals.value: The retry policy is a versioned JSON document in Redis (relay:retry-policy) with one rule per failure class and a bounded history of changes. Every worker process reads the same policy.
Automated DLQ triage writes to three places: the work queue (resubmits), an escalation stream (needs a human), and the retry policy. Only the escalation stream needs manual review.

decisions.statement: The initial policy reproduces Relay's pre-STORY-008 behavior (every class retried 3 times); triage moves it toward the runbook's table as real DLQ entries are seen.
decisions.rationale: the policy changes because of observed failures, not because of a guess made up front, and deploying this story alone changes no retry behavior.

decisions.statement: A rule's action (retry/discard/escalate) governs DLQ handling; for live retries only discard cuts attempts to 1. Escalate still retries live.
decisions.rationale: found while running the demo: treating escalate as 'no live retries' would have silently stopped retrying every unknown error, a behavior change nobody asked for. An unknown error may be transient; it just needs a human once it reaches the DLQ.

decisions.statement: Codified rules only make retries more conservative or slower (discard, longer backoff, capped). They never raise attempts, and withReliability's maxRetries stays the hard ceiling.
decisions.rationale: an automated policy that can grow retries without bound would turn one bad upstream into a retry storm.

decisions.statement: Policy updates use optimistic WATCH/MULTI with recompute-on-conflict, and calls on one store instance are queued because WATCH is per connection.
decisions.rationale: several triagers or worker processes can update the policy at once; a plain read-modify-write would lose updates.

limitations.statement: No standing triage worker loops over the DLQ; triageNextDlqEntry is called by code (tests, demo, a script).
DLQ entries store only the failure message, so a failure whose HTTP status isn't in the message text classifies as unclassified and is escalated.
The STORY-006 worker loop does not make external calls, so policy-driven retries apply where callExternalApiAndPersist is given a retryPolicy, not inside the autoscaled workers yet.
